title: Endgame ramp + intervention log
content:
Purpose: capture decisions and immediate interventions during the v1.8.3 endgame ramp and the follow-up hotfix triage. This is a working log — expect updates and stamped action items.

Attendees: Maya Chen (owner), Liam O'Connor, Priya Nair, Diego Alvarez, Sarah Kim (observability), Alex Ford (platform).

High-level summary:
- We started ramping traffic to v1.8.3 at 09:15 PT. Canary baseline (5% -> 20%) executed. At ~09:40 PT we observed an increase in 5xx spikes from the canary nodes tied to cache-ttl churn during prefix-cache warmups.
- Immediate mitigation: scaled canary pool down to 8% and enabled conservative prefix-caching TTLs for the canary subset. Reverted in-flight autoscaler override (PR#987) — re-evaluate after stabilization.
- Root-cause hypothesis: a race between cache invalidation job and the new KV-cache compaction path introduced in Serving Runtime change set ENG-4521. Compaction leads to transient cache misses, causing higher backend load on embeddings gateway when sequence lengths are short.

Timeline (notes taken live):
- 09:10: Canary plan readout; no blockers.
- 09:15: Traffic shifted to 5% canary. Metrics baseline OK.
- 09:30: Increased canary to 20% per ramp plan.
- 09:39: Observability alert: spike in 500s (rate +18% over baseline) from canary pool. Error group: cache-lookup-timeout in embeddings path.
- 09:42: Rolled canary back to 8% and toggled conservative caching flag (runtime flag: prefix_cache.strict_ttl=true).
- 09:55: 500s reduced to +4% over baseline. Continue monitoring.
- 10:05: Decided to block full ramp until hotfix validated in staging.

Immediate action items (owners + due):
- Maya: open hotfix branch for compaction race and add deterministic unit test for prefix eviction. Target: 2025-02-11 EOD. Linked: ENG-4599.
- Priya: coordinate a quick benchmark run on staging with synthetic short-seq workload (95th token lengths < 64) and attach perf traces. Target: 2025-02-11 14:00 PT.
- Liam: roll a canary with instrumentation to capture KV-cache metrics (eviction rate, compaction cycles) and forward to observability dashboard (dashboard id in Confluence page). Target: 2025-02-11 12:00 PT.
- Diego: prepare a rollback checklist for Dedicated capacity customers on v1.8.3 in case of late degradation. Include contact list and runbook. Target: 2025-02-12 10:00 PT.
- Sarah: create alert TTL change proposal and adjust SLO threshold for canary 95th latency for the next 72 hours. Target: 2025-02-11 09:00 PT.

Decisions made:
- Do not proceed with global ramp beyond 20% until hotfix branch passes synthetic workloads and internal perf gate.
- Keep autoscaler override disabled for canary nodes; let default scaling policy operate. Manual intervention only on confirmed mitigation.
- For v1.8.3 changelog, add explicit note about cache compaction opt-in and guidance for customers using short-sequence traffic patterns.

Risks & mitigations:
- Risk: Customer-facing latency regressions on short-sequence embeddings-heavy workloads. Mitigation: Notify top-5 Dedicated customers (Diego) with rollback window; enable temporary traffic pin to previous minor version if hit.
- Risk: Observability blindspots for compact/evict cycles. Mitigation: Liam to add new instrumentation points and synthetic trace IDs to reproduce.

Open questions (need answers before next sync):
- Is there a safe default TTL value that prevents the compaction churn without materially increasing memory pressure for large deployments? (Priya to propose and test.)
- Can the compaction be made cooperative with the cache-invalidation job (lock-free handoff) or do we need a serialization barrier? (Maya to propose implementation tradeoffs in hotfix branch.)

Notes for release notes / changelog team:
- Tag change: "KV cache compaction (experimental) - enabled via runtime flag; known interactions with short-seq workloads."
- Add a troubleshooting subsection: "If you observe increased 5xx or higher tail latency after upgrading, follow rollback steps and contact release-engineering@redwood.com."

Follow-ups and next meeting:
- Short sync tomorrow (2025-02-11 11:00 PT) to review hotfix CI results and staging perf.
- Full endgame retro scheduled Fri 2025-02-14 10:00 PT to capture timeline and draft postmortem if hotfix was required.

Misc (notes-to-self and scratch):
- Slack: #release-endgame had a buried thread at 09:47 that called out a second error group (identity-tag mismatch) — correlate with rollout metadata.
- Consider adding a tiny canary that only exercises prefix-caching path (no external model calls) to decouple infra vs model flakiness.
- When writing postmortem, prefer timeline + hypothesis + evidence + fix plan; keep blame-free language.

End of log.
